set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR public works coverage determinations PW 2006-001 (Horizons at Indio, March 12, 2007) and PW 2006-018 (Crossings at Madera), following PW 2004-016 (Rancho Santa Fe Village): publicly offered conduit multifamily housing revenue bonds are not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) because proceeds and repayments never enter the issuer's coffers, and are not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4); even if they were, the affordable housing loan exemption (now 1720(c)(5)(E), 40% of units at or below 80% AMI for 20 years) would apply. Current 1720 text contains no conduit bond trigger. Applies to the County bond issuance only; any County A1, Measure W, HOME or other loans in the same deal are analyzed separately.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false for bond issuance alone based on DIR coverage determinations on point (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf, https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-018.pdf). Privately placed bond structures were not separately confirmed; layered public loans can still trigger coverage.

reason: DIR coverage determinations hold that conduit housing revenue bonds are not public funds under Labor Code 1720, so the bond issuance alone does not trigger prevailing wage.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found. A fee waived or reduced by a political subdivision is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), but whether a categorical AHIF exemption is a waiver, and whether coverage follows, depends on 1720(c)(3) de minimis limits (under $600,000 and under 2% of project cost) and project facts; the 1720(c)(5)(E) affordable housing exemption covers below-market loans only, not fee waivers. AHIF revenue spent through Oakland NOFA loans is governed by the NOFA terms, not this record.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear. Only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) public funds definition, with outcome dependent on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. No DIR determination on an affordable housing impact fee exemption was located.

reason: No Oakland ordinance provision, NOFA term or DIR determination states whether the AHIF exemption triggers prevailing wage; only the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) definition applies, so left unclear after reading Labor Code 1720 and searching DIR coverage determinations.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: HCD Prohousing Incentive Program guidelines (Round 4 and October 2026 final guidelines) and the Round 4 and Round 5 NOFAs contain no prevailing wage provision. PIP funds pass to projects as City grants or loans for capitalized service reserves, so coverage depends on the general Labor Code 1720(b) public funds definition, 1720(c) exemptions (including 1720(c)(5)(E) for qualifying below-market loans) and project facts.
set.next_deadline: HCD PIP Round 5 NOFA released October 13, 2026 (about $8 million statewide); applications due March 31, 2027, Prohousing Designation required by March 31, 2027, awards expected June 2027. Oakland Round 4 result not confirmed.
set.cycle_notes: State PIP rounds funded from SB 2 Building Homes and Jobs Trust Fund collections; Round 5 NOFA October 13, 2026 with March 31, 2027 due date.

reason: HCD PIP guidelines and NOFAs (Round 4, 2026 guidelines, Round 5) contain no prevailing wage rule, so coverage rests only on general Labor Code 1720 and project facts; deadline updated to the Round 5 due date.
